intro: What the Omarchy Mac kernel (linux-aurora) and boot loader (m1n1) drive on every Apple Silicon MacBook: 42 boards from M1 to M6, including MacBook Neo. The board list comes from Apple's model identification pages and AppleDB, so models with no code yet are included.

Every status comes from code: the board's compiled device tree, a matching kernel driver, and any per-board gate in the driver or m1n1. On means the code is present and enabled by default. It does not mean the feature has passed hardware testing; results live in Omarchy M+ — Hardware testing and validation.
summary: M1 to M2 Max (13 boards): every device has a driver; display and GPU are on by default. The gap is external display on M2 (USB-C DisplayPort node disabled).

M3 (7 of 9 boards): native display and GPU on by default on J504, J613, J615, J514S, J516S, J516C and J514C. J514C became default with m1n1#31; its GPU power values are copied from the 16" and unqualified. On M3 Pro only the 12-core CPU / 18-core GPU bin gets the GPU; the 14-core GPU bin loads a firmware the kernel does not pin yet (linux-aurora#366, #390).

Power + sleep: sleep is s2idle only on every board; there is no deep sleep. cpufreq and cpuidle are present on M1 to M3 and Neo, and missing on M4 to M6. Measured sleep drain: M1 Pro J314S 2.25 W, M3 Pro J514S 1.35 W, about 2 W on an M2 Pro, against 0.25 W for macOS on the same M1 Pro. Neo does not resume from s2idle yet.

Binned M3 Max (T6034): J514M display and GPU are merged in the kernel (linux-aurora#408) and Mesa (mesa#33), and go on by default when m1n1#32 merges (approved). J516M has nothing yet and boots on the basic framebuffer.
MacBook Neo: display, GPU, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and audio on by default. External display and Touch ID partial.

Every M4, M5 and M6 MacBook (19 boards) is not installable. 15 have no device tree. J604, J713, J715 and J813 have one with no storage controller. Only the 14" M5 Max J714C has open bring-up PRs (linux-aurora#404).

basecamp.common_note: The Common hardware column covers storage, keyboard and trackpad, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, speakers, headphone jack and microphones, USB-C and Thunderbolt, camera, video decode, battery and sensors. It lists only the items that are not On.
evidence: Each board's .dts was preprocessed and compiled, and every node's effective status read (a node is off if it or a parent is disabled). Each enabled node's compatible strings or PCI ID were matched against drivers/ and sound/. All 27 existing MacBook device trees bind a driver for every enabled device, so every gap comes from a per-board gate or an undescribed device.

GPU: the driver's device matches (drm/asahi/driver.rs:164-218) cover t8103, t8112, t600x, t602x, t8122, t6030, t6031, t6040 and t8140; the G15 driver (g15/mod.rs:143-157) covers t6030, t6031 and t6034. M3 Air and J504 are admitted by asahi/m3/t8122_admission.rs:9, M3 Pro by asahi/g15/glue.c:229 with one pinned firmware TEXT per board (g15/hw.rs:156-171; the 14-core GPU bin's cd05af6a… image is added by linux-aurora#366 and #390), J516C by g15/hw/t6031.rs:183 and J514C by g15/boot.rs:475 (linux-aurora#363) and J514M by g15/boot.rs:479 (linux-aurora#408); boot.rs:497 refuses every other T6034 board. m1n1 turns graphics on by default for J613, J615, J504, J514S, J516S, J516C and J514C (kboot.c:407-419, J514C added by m1n1#31).

Display: M1/M2 use the standard DCP driver. M3 boards need an entry in drm/apple/iomfb_v14_7.c:231-239: T6030 (any M3 Pro), J613, J615, J504 (linux-aurora#388), J516C, J514C and J514M. External displays are native on M3 Pro through the device tree's dispext handoff (dcp.c:1385), need chosen.asahi,t8122-dcpext=1 on J613 (m1n1 kboot.c:2785), are not wired on J615 and J504 because only t8122-j613.dts describes the USB-C routes to dcpext (J615 routes in linux-aurora#356), and have no nodes on M3 Max (linux-aurora#292).
Speakers: every MacBook has speakers enabled in sound/soc/apple/macaudio.c:1862, directly or through a compatible fallback. They still need the speakersafetyd daemon in userspace.

Touch ID: the SEP driver (drivers/soc/apple/sep.rs) provides enrol and verify through /dev/sep-bio. SEP nodes ship disabled by design and the driver enables them at runtime (sep.rs:10). A board is covered when soc/apple/profile.rs:550-590 has a profile (T8103, T6000/T6001, T6020/T6021, T8112, T8140, and T8122 for J613/J615 only) and its fingerprint sensor node is enabled: every M1, M1 Pro/Max, M2, M2 Pro/Max and M3 Air MacBook, and Neo. M3 Pro SEP is in linux-aurora#282. Touch ID still needs userspace integration.

M4 Pro and later: board codes and chip IDs come from Apple's MacBook Pro and MacBook Air pages and AppleDB. m1n1 has only CPU start code for T604x and T605x. M6 work so far targets the Mac mini J873G (linux-aurora#191 to #198, #359). AppleDB gives M5 Pro and M5 Max the same chip ID (0x6050) while m1n1 also defines T6051, so whether M5 Max splits across two chips like M3 Max is not confirmed.

Power + sleep: each cell gives code evidence first and lab results second, labelled Code and Lab. Partial means the code paths exist but sleep is s2idle only and drains far more than macOS. cpufreq is an enabled *-cluster-cpufreq node with a driver match. cpuidle starts on t8103, t8112, t8122, t600x, t602x, t6030, t6031, t6032, t6034 and t8140 (drivers/cpuidle/cpuidle-apple.c:173-186; WFI only on T8140), and on no M4, M5 or M6 chip. Apple Silicon has no PSCI system suspend, so mem_sleep offers only s2idle. The display driver has system-sleep handlers for every generation (drm/apple/dcp.c:5086). The GPU driver has none, because its firmware stays resident; on T6031, genpd powers the GPU domain off under it, which linux-aurora#288 fixes (open).

Power lab sources: M1 Pro J314S figures are 5 V input measurements from 14 Oct 2026; a live Thunderbolt link adds about 1.3 W in sleep there. The M3 Pro J514S figure is the SMC coulomb counter on battery, from linux-aurora#274. The M2 Pro figure is from the 9 Oct 2026 battery investigation (board not recorded). The Neo resume status comes from the linux-aurora#227 qualification notes.

Not covered by code evidence: backlight and fn keys, sustained power and thermals. The 28 Oct test reports still fail display controller, backlight, ambient light, fn key and external display checks on every M3 board that reported.
